dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:101.text: Jade of three colors. Formed from 玉, with 無 indicating the sound.

shuowen:102.text: Decayed jade. Formed from 玉, with 有 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 畜 in 畜牧, livestock husbandry.

shuowen:103.text: Beautiful jade. Formed from 玉, with 睿 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “A jade cap and jade tassels.”

shuowen:104.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 求 indicating the sound.

shuowen:105.text: Beautiful jade. Formed from 玉, with 林 indicating the sound.

shuowen:106.text: A round ceremonial jade. Formed from 玉, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:107.text: A jade disc with a large hole, used to assist a ruler ascending steps. Formed from 玉, with 爰 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “When the hole is twice the solid rim, it is 瑗; when the rim is twice the hole, it is 璧.”

shuowen:108.text: A jade disc; when rim and hole are equal, it is called 環. Formed from 玉, with 睘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:109.text: Half a jade disc. Formed from 玉, with 黃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:110.text: A ceremonial jade, eight inches across, resembling a chariot's axle bushing. Formed from 玉, with 宗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:111.text: A ceremonial jade for dispatching troops, patterned as a tiger. Formed from 玉 and 虎; 虎 also indicates the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “He bestowed a pair of 琥 on Zijia.”

shuowen:112.text: A jade used in prayers during drought, bearing a dragon pattern. Formed from 玉 and 龍; 龍 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:113.text: A jade tablet with a rounded end. Formed from 玉, with 宛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:114.text: A tablet sharpened at the top is 圭; half a 圭 is 璋. Formed from 玉, with 章 indicating the sound. The Rites lists six paired gifts: 圭 with horses, 璋 with hides, 璧 with silk, 琮 with brocade, 琥 with embroidery, 璜 with axe-patterned cloth.

shuowen:115.text: Beautiful coloring rising on a jade disc. Formed from 玉, with 炎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:116.text: A large jade tablet. Formed from 玉, with 介 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “He raised and respectfully presented a great jade tablet.”

shuowen:117.text: A jade tablet one foot two inches long, fitted with a libation ladle for sacrifices in the ancestral temple. Formed from 玉, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:118.text: The 桓 jade tablet held by dukes. Formed from 玉, with 獻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:119.text: A great jade tablet, three feet long, tapered above, with a mallet-shaped head. Formed from 玉, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:120.text: When feudal lords hold jade tablets in audience with the Son of Heaven, he holds a jade to cap them, resembling a plow's cap. The Rites of Zhou says: “The Son of Heaven holds a four-inch 瑁.” Formed from 玉 and 冒; 冒 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:121.text: A jade pendant. Formed from 玉, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:122.text: The upper jade of a pendant set, used to regulate walking and stopping. Formed from 玉, with 行 indicating the sound.

shuowen:123.text: A jade pendant. Formed from 玉, with 夬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:124.text: To use jade as a token of authority. Formed from 玉 and 耑.

shuowen:125.text: An ear ornament. Formed from 玉 and 耳; 耳 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:126.text: To fill the ears with jade ornaments. Formed from 玉, with 眞 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Those jade ear ornaments!”

shuowen:127.text: The upper fitting of a worn knife. The Son of Heaven uses jade; feudal lords use gold. Formed from 玉, with 奉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:128.text: The lower fitting of a worn knife. The Son of Heaven uses jade. Formed from 玉, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:129.text: Jade on a sword's suspension lug. Formed from 玉, with 彘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:130.text: Jade claws on a carriage canopy. Formed from 玉, with 蚤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:131.text: Raised patterned carving on jade tablets and discs. Formed from 玉, with abbreviated 篆 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Carved jade tablets and discs.”

shuowen:132.text: The carved pattern on a 琮 jade. Formed from 玉, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:133.text: Cap ornamentation, capped here and there with jade. Formed from 玉, with 綦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:134.text: Jade ornamentation patterned like aquatic plants. Formed from 玉, with 喿 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Aquatic plants, fire and grains of rice.”

shuowen:135.text: Hanging jade ornaments of a ceremonial crown. Formed from 玉, with 流 indicating the sound.

shuowen:136.text: A jade vessel. Formed from 玉, with 𠷎 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 淑.

shuowen:137.text: A jade vessel. Formed from 玉, with 畾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:138.text: Bright white jade coloring. Formed from 玉, with 差 indicating the sound.

shuowen:139.text: Brilliant jade coloring. Formed from 玉, with 此 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The new terrace has brilliance.”

shuowen:140.text: Jade's brilliance linked together like the strings of a zither. Formed from 玉, with 瑟 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Lustrous is that jade libation ladle.”

shuowen:141.text: Jade's brilliance arrayed in orderly ranks. Formed from 玉, with 㮚 indicating the sound. The Lost Analects says: “The jade glitters lustrously; its 𤩰 is vigorous.” [The final description is uncertain.]

shuowen:142.text: The coloring of jade. Formed from 玉, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound. Another explanation: stone next in quality to jade. The Lost Analects says: “Like the luster of jade.”

shuowen:143.text: Reddish jade coloring. Formed from 玉, with 㒼 indicating the sound. Red grain seedlings are called 虋; 璊 says the jade's color resembles them.

shuowen:144.text: A small red blemish in jade. Formed from 玉, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:145.text: To work jade. Formed from 玉, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:146.text: To work jade. Another explanation: stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:147.text: To work jade. Formed from 玉, with 里 indicating the sound.

shuowen:148.text: A treasure. Formed from 玉, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:149.text: To play with or handle. Formed from 玉, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:150.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:151.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 倉 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The leather reins ring with ornaments.”

shuowen:152.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 丁 indicating the sound. Ji, son of Taigong of Qi, was posthumously called Duke 玎.

shuowen:153.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 爭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:154.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 𧴪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:155.text: The sound of jade. Formed from 玉, with 皇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:156.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 禹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:157.text: Stone next in quality to jade, used to suspend a jade disc. Formed from 玉, with 丰 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 菶菶 in the Odes' “Melons and little melons flourish.” Another pronunciation is like 蚌 in 𧊧蚌.

shuowen:158.text: 玪𤨙: stone next in quality to jade. Formed from 玉, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:159.text: The stone called 玪𤨙. Formed from 玉, with 勒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:160.text: The jade ornament 瓊琚. Formed from 玉, with 居 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “I repay it with 瓊琚.”

shuowen:161.text: Stone next in quality to jade. Formed from 玉, with 莠 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Ear ornaments of 璓 and 瑩.”

shuowen:162.text: A black stone next in quality to jade. Formed from 玉, with 久 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “She gives me pendant 玖.” Pronounced like 芑; some say like 句 in “a person's bent spine,” 句脊.

shuowen:163.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 𦣞 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 貽.

shuowen:164.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 艮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:165.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 曳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:166.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 巢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:167.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 進 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 津.

shuowen:168.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 朁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:169.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 悤 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 蔥.

shuowen:170.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 號 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 鎬.

shuowen:171.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 舝 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 曷.

shuowen:172.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 𥄗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:173.text: Stone next in quality to jade. Formed from 玉, with 燮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:174.text: Stone next in quality to jade. Formed from 玉, with 句 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 苟.

shuowen:175.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 言 indicating the sound.

shuowen:176.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 盡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:177.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 隹 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 維.

shuowen:178.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 烏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:179.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 眉 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 眉.

shuowen:180.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:181.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 厶 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 私.

shuowen:182.text: Stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 于 indicating the sound.

shuowen:183.text: A kind of jade. Formed from 玉, with 𠬸 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 沒.

shuowen:184.text: A black stone resembling jade. Formed from 玉, with 皆 indicating the sound. Pronounced like 諧.

shuowen:185.text: Beautiful blue-green stone. Formed from 玉 and 石, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:186.text: Beautiful stone. Formed from 玉, with 昆 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Yangzhou offers 瑤 and 琨 as tribute.”

shuowen:187.text: Beautiful stone. Formed from 玉, with 民 indicating the sound.

shuowen:188.text: Beautiful jade. Formed from 玉, with 䍃 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “I repay it with 瓊瑤.”

shuowen:189.text: The yin essence of a clam. Formed from 玉, with 朱 indicating the sound. This is what the Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States means by “Pearls ward off fire disasters.”

shuowen:190.text: 玓瓅: the brilliance of a luminous pearl. Formed from 玉, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:191.text: The brilliance called 玓瓅. Formed from 玉, with 樂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:192.text: A pearl. Formed from 玉, with 比 indicating the sound. Song Hong says: “玭 pearls occur in the Huai River.” 玭 is a pearl that makes a sound.

shuowen:193.text: A kind of clam. Formed from 玉, with 劦 indicating the sound. The Rites says: “For a scholar's worn knife, the upper fitting is 珕 and the lower 珧.”

shuowen:194.text: A clam shell, used to ornament objects. Formed from 玉, with 兆 indicating the sound. The Rites says: “For the Son of Heaven's worn knife, the upper fitting is jade and the lower 珧.”

shuowen:195.text: The precious material 火齊, namely 玫瑰. Another explanation: beautiful stone. Formed from 玉, with 文 indicating the sound.

shuowen:196.text: The precious stone 玟瑰. Formed from 玉, with 鬼 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a round central hole.

shuowen:197.text: A pearl that is not round. Formed from 玉, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:198.text: 琅玕: something resembling pearls. Formed from 玉, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:199.text: The material 琅玕. Formed from 玉, with 干 indicating the sound. The Tribute of Yu says: “Yongzhou: 球, 琳 and 琅玕.”

shuowen:200.text: Coral: red, growing in the sea, or sometimes in mountains. Formed from 玉, with abbreviated 刪 indicating the sound.
